extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media partners, donors, and the general public interested in investigative reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational principles and operating standards used by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) to guide the production, collaboration, and dissemination of large-scale cross-border investigative reporting. Focuses on transparency, collaboration, impact, security, and data-driven methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: To show people how the world really works through stories that rock the world; forcing positive change
rubrics_metrics.description: To show people how the world really works through stories that rock the world; forcing positive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICIJ's reporting should reveal systemic wrongdoing and power abuses with the goal of triggering positive change; projects are framed by public interest and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision: We expose wrongdoing so the world can make it right
rubrics_metrics.description: We expose wrongdoing so the world can make it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should focus on exposing corruption, abuses of power and grave harms inflicted on vulnerable people, with the intention of informing corrective action and reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency is at the center of everything we do
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency is at the center of everything we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should prioritize independently-sourced facts and openness in methods and findings to support credibility and democratic accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest focus and countering misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Vital public interest reporting must compete against a flood of misinformation that confuses, alienates and divides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be designed to cut through noise and misinformation — emphasizing clarity, sourcing, and relevance to public welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Largest cross-border reporting initiatives and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Directed the largest cross-border reporting initiatives in history, convincing reporters across the globe to set aside traditional rivalries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer large-scale, cross-border collaboration with many media partners to pool expertise, languages and reach; collaboration is a core methodological standard (e.g., Panama Papers, Pandora Papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: No-pay model for media partners; reliance on donations
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ relies entirely on donations to fund our work. We do not pay media partners. Nor do they pay us for publishing our projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationally, projects are funded by donors and distributed freely through partner outlets; financial independence from commercial arrangements with media partners is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact-driven reporting (triggering legal, policy and societal changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work has shaken the establishment and led to public protests, multiple arrests, sweeping legal reform and official inquiries in more than 70 countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success is measured by tangible impact (policy change, legal actions, resignations, legislative reforms) as well as awards and public response; projects should be scoped for potential real-world consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and ambition: large document trawls and multi-language work
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations involved separate teams of hundreds of reporters spread across 80 countries, working in more than 30 languages and combing through more than 25 million documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology favors massive data/document analysis, multilingual capacity and broad geographical coverage when warranted by the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cutting-edge tools, machine learning and data techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: We build and maintain cutting-edge tools that can pick apart massive and complex data sets, using machine learning and other aspects of artificial intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical rigor and tooling (data processing, ML, interactive visuals) are standards for handling large datasets and extracting verifiable findings; technology is also shared freely with other journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer scrutiny and networked accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration promotes greater accuracy and depth in our work, through peer scrutiny across cultural, linguistic and journalistic traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should be reviewed and scrutinized by a distributed network of trusted journalists to reduce bias and errors; peer review across partners is a quality-control standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and security for journalists and suppressed stories
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide a layer of security to journalists and media outlets in an era when press freedoms are under attack. Stories suppressed in one country can appear in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational practices must include measures to protect journalists and enable publication in contexts where press freedom is constrained; consider secure communication, publication strategies and partner selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and capacity-building
rubrics_metrics.description: We train hundreds of reporters each year, many from poorer countries. ICIJ also contributes to conferences and events, passing on tips and techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in skill-building and dissemination of methods as part of the organization's standard practice; capacity-building increases quality and global representativeness of investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ’s commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion: ICIJ acknowledges the value that each member of our team brings and commits to further promoting and leveraging a richness of backgrounds and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and organizational decisions should promote diverse perspectives and equitable participation to strengthen journalistic quality and representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network of trusted journalists by invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ retains a network of trusted journalists, which has grown by invitation to more than 290 of the best investigative reporters from more than 100 countries and territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and participation of collaborators is selective and trust-based; maintaining a vetted network is a standard for ensuring reliability and safeguarding sensitive projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making findings available and relevant to billions
rubrics_metrics.description: Our earth-shaking stories about injustice and abuse of power are made available — and relevant — to billions of people each time we publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissemination strategy should aim for maximal public reach and relevance, leveraging partner outlets of varying sizes to ensure broad access to findings.
